To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sensing limitations can be used by the evader to escape from the pursuer.

(i) in the open plane, the evader is able to increase its distance to the pursuers indefinitely, and (ii) in a circular area, the evader may be captured if and only if α < π/4, where α is the sensing uncertainty of the Lion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of sensing uncertainty on the outcome of pursuit-evasion games.
the impact of imperfect sensing on pursuit-evasion games.
the effect of sensing limitations on pursuit evasion games.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sensing uncertainty is always a disadvantage for the pursuer, but the rate of increase of the distance between the players depends on the sensing uncertainty model.
the sensing limitations introduced by an adversarial sensing noise can be exploited to evade capture indefinitely in pursuit-evasion games.
when sensing uncertainty is present, there is no guarantee that an evader can be captured, and if it can be captured, the capture time is not bounded.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evader can always evade a pursuer with bearing uncertainty.
when sensing uncertainty is considered, the pursuer cannot capture the evader in the Lion-and-Man game.
when sensing uncertainty is present, a Lion can never capture the Man.
The main takeaway from our work is that
even when the sensing uncertainty is small, the evader may have a substantial advantage over the pursuer.
sensing limitations can have a dramatic effect on pursuit-evasion games, even for simple sensing models.
even when the pursuer has a deterministic strategy to capture an evading player, sensing limitations may render the pursuer unable to capture the evading player.
